models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light, benign pattern over the Aeolians now - but the forecast ends 1 Oct, three days short of our first leg.
briefing.synopsis: The current picture is a slack, low-gradient regime: land- and sea-breeze dominated mornings, a brief westerly of 9-11 kt around midday 25 Sep, then a light NE-to-N flow of roughly 6-10 kt settling in through 26-27 Sep (consensus of ECMWF IFS 0.25 and AIFS, both 25 Sep runs, with ICON-2i 2 km, 25 Sep 00Z, in the near field). Seas stay small throughout - 0.3 to 2.0 ft total wave and swell at or below 1.7 ft across all six islands. The model data runs out at 23:00 on 1 Oct; our first leg is 4 Oct, so nothing here is a forecast for the trip - treat it purely as a read on the season's current pattern.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: No fleet berth tonight - boats are not yet on the water. For reference, the dry-run scoring puts Portorosa Marina as fully sheltered for the night of 25 Sep, an enclosed basin with all-round protection, and the same exercise gives Porto Pignataro at Lipari, Drautto at Panarea, Pecorini a Mare at Filicudi and Porto Santa Marina at Salina as sheltered on their respective nights. The one berth that scores only 'workable' in the dry run is Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli, open from every direction, where shelter depends entirely on the calm holding - that is the berth to re-check hardest once the real dates come into range.

passage_notes.note: Dry run 26 Sep: 8.1 kt beam reach, scored go. Real date 4 Oct is beyond the data.
Dry run 27 Sep: 8.5 kt head to wind, motoring leg, scored go. Real date 5 Oct not forecast.
Dry run 28 Sep: 2.3 kt broad reach - effectively a motor. Scored go.
Dry run 29 Sep: 1.9 kt, gusts to 6 kt. Calm, scored go.
Dry run 30 Sep: 2.6 kt close reach, gusts to 10 kt. Scored go.
Dry run 1 Oct: 2.5 kt dead downwind - end of the data window. Scored go.

cautions: The forecast horizon is 1 Oct 23:00. Every trip date from 4 Oct onward has no model data at all - the dry-run 'go' verdicts are a test of the scoring against live weather, not a forecast for our passages.

Model spread is already meaningful in places: Lipari midday 25 Sep spans 5.2-12.2 kt and Panarea 4.8-14.0 kt between models, and Stromboli 00:00 on 27 Sep spans 8.4-16.6 kt. Where that range appears, treat the mean as indicative only.
Gusts of 33.2 kt appear at Filicudi and Stromboli at midday 25 Sep against 7-11 kt means. These are IFS interval-maximum values in light air and are reported, not treated as a squall signal.
Stromboli's Marina del Gabbiano is open from every direction in the berth scoring - fine in the current calm, no margin if the pattern changes.
briefing.confidence_note: Near-term run-to-run stability is good - mean wind shift 1.0-1.3 kt out to 120 h across 23 snapshots - but direction shift grows to 53 degrees by 72-120 h, and the trip dates lie entirely beyond the data, so confidence for the voyage itself is low by definition.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
